stories.headline: US Army Orders 2,500+ Skydio X10D Drones for $52M in Largest Single-Vendor sUAS Buy

key_facts.fact: The US Army placed an order exceeding $52 million for over 2,500 X10D drones from Skydio, the largest single-vendor small unmanned aircraft system procurement in Army history.
key_facts.excerpt: Skydio today announced an order exceeding $52 million for over 2,500 X10D drones from the U.S. Army. The order is the largest small unmanned aircraft system (sUAS) procurement from a single manufacturer in the Army's history.

key_facts.fact: The contract moved from bid to award in under 72 hours, bypassing multi-year Pentagon acquisition timelines, placed through Atlantic Diving Supply (ADS).
key_facts.excerpt: The contract moved from bid to award in under 72 hours, bypassing the multi-year acquisition timelines that have defined Pentagon drone procurement for decades. The order was placed through Atlantic Diving Supply (ADS).

key_facts.fact: At nearly 3,000 units, the implied per-unit cost is roughly $17,300, well below the $16,000-$25,000 range previously reported for public safety deployments.
key_facts.excerpt: At nearly 3,000 units, the implied per-unit cost runs roughly $17,300, well below the $16,000 to $25,000 range DroneXL has reported for the X10 platform in public safety deployments.

key_facts.fact: The X10D flies autonomously without GPS using onboard navigation cameras, features multiband radio for contested environments, and has high-resolution visual and thermal cameras for day/night ISR.
key_facts.excerpt: capable of flying autonomously, without GPS, using onboard navigation cameras to map terrain in real time and maintain flight in contested environments. Its multiband radio provides seamless connectivity by optimizing frequency use in high-interference areas.

key_facts.fact: Skydio CEO Adam Bry said the X10D was 'sharpened by hard lessons in Ukraine' and serves as a 'hunter' drone to find targets for other systems.
key_facts.excerpt: Bry was direct about where the X10D learned its most important lessons. 'X10D was sharpened by hard lessons in Ukraine and close iterative feedback with our soldiers through initiatives like the Army's Transformation in Contact.'

key_facts.fact: Skydio is the only manufacturer selected for the Army's SRR Program of Record in both 2022 and 2025, and is trusted by every US military branch and 29 allied nations.
key_facts.excerpt: Skydio is trusted by every branch of the U.S. military and by 29 allied nations. The Army selected Skydio for the SRR Program of Record in both 2022 and 2025, making it the only manufacturer to span both tranches.

stories.headline: SpaceX Launches 29 Starlink Satellites from Cape Canaveral on Record-Setting Booster

key_facts.fact: SpaceX launched a Falcon 9 rocket carrying 29 Starlink V2 Mini satellites from Space Launch Complex 40 at Cape Canaveral on Sunday, March 22, at 10:47 AM EDT.
key_facts.excerpt: Liftoff from Space Launch Complex 40 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station is scheduled for Sunday, March 22, at 10:47 a.m. EDT (1447 UTC).

key_facts.fact: The first-stage booster, designated B1078, launched for its 27th time and successfully landed on the drone ship 'A Shortfall of Gravitas' in the Atlantic Ocean.
key_facts.excerpt: The first-stage booster for this mission, 1078, launching for a 27th time, will land on SpaceX's drone ship 'A Shortfall of Gravitas', stationed in the Atlantic Ocean.

key_facts.fact: The mission, designated Starlink 10-62, took a north-easterly trajectory and brought SpaceX to 840 Starlink satellites launched so far in 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: Spacecraft separation is expected a little more than an hour after liftoff, bringing SpaceX up to a total of 840 Starlink satellites launched so far.

key_facts.fact: Starlink now has an estimated 10.9 million subscribers across 159 countries as of March 23, 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: As of March 23, 2026, @Starlink has an estimated 10,914,680 subscribers. Starlink is now available in 159 countries, territories or other markets around the world.

stories.headline: Draganfly and Palladyne AI Validate Autonomous Drone Swarm Platform for US Defense

key_facts.fact: Draganfly and Palladyne AI announced successful testing of Palladyne's SwarmOS platform across Draganfly's mission-ready drone components, validated through a flight simulation.
key_facts.excerpt: The companies have successfully tested Palladyne AI's SwarmOS platform across Draganfly's mission-ready drone components and validated the system through completion of a successful flight simulation.

key_facts.fact: The integrated system uses a Decentralized Edge Collaborative Autonomy (DECA) approach enabling drones to independently perceive, decide, and collaborate without centralized control or pre-programmed flight paths.
key_facts.excerpt: Unlike conventional drone automation systems that rely on centralized control or pre-programmed flight paths, the integrated solution is designed to enable decentralized, real-time collaboration between drones operating in dynamic and contested environments.

key_facts.fact: The milestone positions Draganfly to pursue demanding US defense programs requiring autonomous swarm capabilities.
key_facts.excerpt: This milestone represents a significant step toward enabling advanced autonomous swarm capabilities for U.S. defense applications.

key_facts.fact: Draganfly CEO Cameron Chell said the system enables 'true autonomous collaboration where systems can think, adapt, and operate together in real time.'
key_facts.excerpt: 'What excites us about this joint effort is the ability to enable true autonomous collaboration where systems that can think, adapt, and operate together in real time.'

sources.title: Draganfly and Palladyne AI Achieve Integration Milestone Advancing Autonomous Swarm Capabilities

stories.headline: Waymo Robotaxi Caught Driving Wrong Way in Houston, Adding to Safety Concerns

key_facts.fact: A Waymo driverless vehicle was captured on dashcam attempting to drive the wrong way down a Houston street near the HOV lane off St. Joseph Parkway, forcing surrounding drivers to maneuver around it.
key_facts.excerpt: Safety concerns are growing after a Waymo driverless vehicle was caught attempting to drive the wrong way down a Houston street. The incident, captured on dashcam and shared with local outlet KHOU, reportedly took place near the HOV lane off St. Joseph Parkway.

key_facts.fact: After the vehicle stopped, a remote Waymo team assisted in backing it up and clearing the intersection.
key_facts.excerpt: Waymo later stated that after the vehicle stopped, a remote team assisted in backing it up and clearing the intersection.

key_facts.fact: Waymo pointed to safety data from Austin showing its vehicles have been involved in 84% fewer airbag-deployment crashes than human drivers.
key_facts.excerpt: The company also pointed to safety data from Austin, claiming its vehicles have been involved in 84% fewer airbag-deployment crashes than human drivers.

key_facts.fact: The incident follows a pattern of Waymo troubles in Texas including a robotaxi appearing to block emergency responders and another narrowly avoiding being hit by a train.
key_facts.excerpt: We have previously covered some of Waymo's trouble in Texas and beyond, from a robotaxi that appeared to block emergency responders to another that narrowly avoided being hit by a train.

stories.headline: Israel's XTEND Signs $11M Deal With India's Rayonix to Manufacture AI-Powered UAVs

key_facts.fact: Israel-based AI robotics firm XTEND signed an $11 million manufacturing and distribution agreement with India's Rayonix Tech to locally produce AI-powered unmanned aerial vehicles.
key_facts.excerpt: Israel-based AI robotics firm XTEND has signed an $11 million manufacturing and distribution agreement with India's Rayonix Tech to produce advanced unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) locally.

key_facts.fact: Rayonix Tech will serve as XTEND's exclusive partner in India, responsible for establishing local manufacturing, testing, and distribution infrastructure.
key_facts.excerpt: Rayonix Tech will act as XTEND's exclusive partner in India, responsible for establishing local manufacturing, testing, and distribution infrastructure.

key_facts.fact: At the core of the partnership is XTEND's XOS operating system, which enables human-guided autonomy allowing operators to control multiple robotic systems simultaneously while leveraging AI for navigation, targeting, and mission execution.
key_facts.excerpt: At the core of this partnership is XTEND's XOS operating system, which will serve as the digital backbone for UAVs produced in India. The platform is designed to enable human-guided autonomy, allowing operators to control multiple robotic systems simultaneously while leveraging AI for navigation, targeting, and mission execution.

key_facts.fact: The deal aligns with India's broader push toward defence indigenisation under 'Make in India' and includes a technology-transfer component.
key_facts.excerpt: The agreement marks a significant development in defence cooperation between Israel and India, especially at a time when autonomous aerial systems are becoming central to battlefield operations worldwide.

stories.headline: Festus, Missouri Advances $6 Billion Data Center Deal Despite Widespread Opposition

key_facts.fact: The City of Festus, Missouri reached a framework development agreement with CRG for a proposed $6 billion data center, representing one of the largest private investments in Jefferson County history.
key_facts.excerpt: The City of Festus, Missouri has reached a 'framework' agreement to move forward with a proposed $6 billion data center, despite widespread opposition from local residents.

key_facts.fact: The project would generate an estimated $1.3 billion in property taxes, utility taxes, and community benefit payments over 25 years, averaging $53 million annually.
key_facts.excerpt: This will be a $6 BILLION initial investment in our community, with an estimated $1.3 BILLION in property taxes, utility taxes, and community benefit payments over 25 years, resulting in an average benefit to the community of over $53 Million annually.

key_facts.fact: The city negotiated $45 million in direct community payments over 10 years plus up to $5 million for a new firehouse, with no real property tax abatement for the data center.
key_facts.excerpt: The City of Festus will receive significant, direct, community benefit payments totaling $45 Million over 10 years, starting at $3 Million in the first year, and also including a payment of up to $5 Million for a new City firehouse.

key_facts.fact: Residents have expressed concerns about noise, light pollution, and impacts on regional water supply; the city council held a public meeting on March 23 at Festus High School gymnasium.
key_facts.excerpt: Some are concerned about noise, light pollution and impacts on the regional water supply. Others have complained about a lack of transparency from local officials.

key_facts.fact: A voluntary buyout program was negotiated for residents in close proximity to the proposed site near Highway 67 and County Road CC.
key_facts.excerpt: the City has negotiated the establishment of a voluntary buyout program, to be administered by CRG, for houses on Glenkee Court, and other eligible houses

stories.headline: US Army 2nd Cavalry Deploys Drone-Launching Ground Robots for Recon in Germany

key_facts.fact: The 2nd Cavalry Regiment is using a two-part unmanned team built around the Project Origin robotic combat vehicle at Grafenwöhr, Germany, where a ground robot deploys an aerial drone from its hatch for reconnaissance.
key_facts.excerpt: They're sitting behind their Strykers, watching a ground robot disappear into the tree line, waiting for a hatch to open and a drone to climb out of it. The enemy command post stays exactly where it is. The soldiers stay exactly where they are. The machines do the dangerous part.

key_facts.fact: The system is the 2nd Cavalry Regiment's current answer to the reconnaissance problem, replacing traditional manned scouting with an 'unmanned edge' approach.
key_facts.excerpt: This is the 2nd Cavalry Regiment's current answer to the reconnaissance problem, and it's called the unmanned edge.

key_facts.fact: The exercises were reported by the 7th Mobile Public Affairs Detachment, with scouts operating from behind Stryker vehicles while machines perform the dangerous reconnaissance tasks.
key_facts.excerpt: In a forest near Grafenwöhr, Germany, the scouts of the 2nd Cavalry Regiment are doing something that would have been science fiction to the cavalrymen who rode these same European roads eighty years ago, as 7th Mobile Public Affairs Detachment reports.

sources.title: 2nd Cavalry Scouts With Drones, Not Soldiers
